title: A determinism check for HiGHS and CP-SAT

blocks.text: A pipeline-inspection company schedules its inspection robots with a small MILP and wants a test that fails the build when a run stops repeating. A run is a function of no arguments that solves the model and returns its manifest, a dict such as `{"status": "OPTIMAL", "objective": 17.0, "plan": [["R1", "seg-4"], ...]}`.

Write `assert_deterministic(run, runs)`. It calls `run` exactly `runs` times and compares every manifest with the first, in the canonical form `canonical(manifest)` that the starter gives you. If they all match, it returns the sha256 hex digest of that canonical form. If any differs, it raises `AssertionError` with a message that names the first run that differs (for example "run 3") and the top-level fields that differ, using `changed_fields(a, b)` from the starter.
The tests run it on a HiGHS model and on a CP-SAT model, and on runs made to change. About ten lines.

cases.says: a HiGHS run and a CP-SAT run pass and return their digest; a run whose objective changes fails
every run is compared with the first, not only the second
the whole manifest is compared, so a tie with another plan fails
the error message names the run and the fields that differ

origin.section: A Determinism Test Belongs in the Test Suite

concepts: every run is compared with the first as canonical bytes, and a difference fails with the changed fields named
